content:
Hi!

I'm new to the mathlib community, cf. my introduction in #new members channel. I'm submitting PR with a version of the Filter.Tendsto.cesaro_smul (Cesàro average converges to same limit as the original sequence) from Mathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/SpecificAsymptotics.lean to apply to general positive weights (with divergent sum). This is useful in several areas for instance to obtain convergence results for stochastic recurrences (hence the general normed spaces framework).

Any feedback/review on this PR #43886 appreciated.

PS. The proof is not using the little O functionality yet, I'm not so verse is such compositional (as opposed to sequential) writing.

I haven't carefully read the code yet, but here is a general advice for AI-assisted code: do have-inversion to clean up the code. Quoting what I suggested in another PR:

For each have, think of the following

  • is it important enough to be its own lemma?
  • Can you eliminate it by changing the proof flow? That is instead of having
have key : keyHypothesis  := A
<B: one line prove with key>

you can write

suffices keyHypothesis by
   <B: one line prove with key>
   -- sometimes you can do `rw`, `apply`, or `refine` to skip `suffices`
A

or even

refine some_existing_lemma ?_ ....
A

PS. The proof is not using the little O functionality yet, cf. some existing problems.

This doesn't look like what a human would say about things, because the "existing problems" you quoted was from porting lean 3 code, which is not a mathematical problem. Could you expand on what you meant by this?

Sure, maybe the writing is not so good, I was rather trying to follow the equations one after another as they unfold in the paper proof and from there got so many errors that I kind of backed off into the safety. If this is really off charts I'll try to make it more fluid, will be a learning experience !

Even leaving LLMs aside, it´s perfectly fined when writing the proof in lean the first time around to have a whole bunch of haves, it's just a question of cleaning up the presentation later, just like in a paper proof for publication
